# Likely Causes for Your Throat, Congestion, and Low Fever

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/thermometer-half.svg

Your symptoms for 3 days fit a few common possibilities:
- **Viral upper respiratory infection**: most likely with sore throat, congestion, and low-grade fever.
- **COVID-19 or flu**: can look very similar early on, especially with fever and throat symptoms.
- **Seasonal allergies plus irritation**: allergies can cause congestion and throat discomfort, but **fever is less typical**, so another cause is more likely.
- **Post-nasal drip**: mucus draining down the throat can worsen soreness and coughing/throat clearing.

## Home Care and Non-Prescription Relief

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg

- **Fluids**: water, warm tea, broth, or electrolyte drinks; aim for pale-yellow urine.
- **Rest**: reduce exertion for a couple of days.
- **Sore throat care**:
  - Warm salt-water gargles 3–4 times daily
  - Honey in tea or by the spoonful if you tolerate it
  - Throat lozenges or hard candies
- **Congestion care**:
  - Saline nasal spray or rinse
  - Humidifier or steamy shower
  - Sleep with your head slightly elevated
- **Fever/headache comfort**:
  - **Acetaminophen** or **ibuprofen** if you normally can take them safely and have no medical reason to avoid them
- **Cetirizine**:
  - Reasonable if allergies are contributing, but it may not help much if this is a virus
  - It can sometimes dry you out, so pair it with hydration

## When to Seek Medical Care

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/exclamation-triangle.svg

Get urgent medical care if you develop:
- **Shortness of breath**
- **Chest pain**
- **Trouble swallowing saliva, drooling, or muffled “hot potato” voice**
- **Severe one-sided throat pain or swelling**
- **High fever** or fever that keeps rising
- **Confusion, severe weakness, or dehydration**
- **Blue lips, worsening wheeze, or lips/face swelling**
- **A stiff neck with severe headache**
- **Symptoms that are clearly worsening instead of slowly improving**

Seek a routine medical visit soon if:
- Fever lasts **more than 3–5 days**
- Sore throat is severe or lasts **more than a week**
- You see **white patches on tonsils**, a widespread rash, or swollen tender neck glands
- You may need testing for **strep, COVID-19, or flu**
- You have repeated sinus pain, ear pain, or thick discharge that persists

## 48-Hour Symptom Check

Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/calendar-check.svg

| Time | What to Track | What Would Be Reassuring | What Would Worry Me |
|---|---|---|---|
| Now | Temperature, throat pain, congestion, headache, energy | Mild fever, able to drink fluids | Fever climbing, worsening throat pain, trouble swallowing |
| 12 hours | Breathing, cough, mucus color, hydration | Breathing normal, drinking okay | New shortness of breath, chest pain, dizziness |
| 24 hours | Fever trend, sore throat, sinus pressure | Fever stable or lower, symptoms not spreading | Fever persists or symptoms clearly worsen |
| 36 hours | Ability to rest, eat, and function | Slight improvement or same | Marked fatigue, dehydration, severe headache |
| 48 hours | Overall direction of illness | Gradual improvement | No improvement or new red flags |

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: COVID test](https://www.cdc.gov/covid/testing/index.html)
Action: [Button: Symptom checker](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/)
Action: [Button: Find urgent care](https://www.healthcare.gov/see-plans/#/)

## Sources

- CDC respiratory illness guidance: https://www.cdc.gov/respiratory-viruses/index.html
- NHS sore throat overview: https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/sore-throat/
- CDC COVID testing information: https://www.cdc.gov/covid/testing/index.html
